fieldValues.title: No clerk act affirms a remedy or problem: affirmation is a hand-run record fork under the owner's actor
fieldValues.summary: clerk session records ratify, set-aside, consider, edit, comment, attendee and transcript. It has no affirm. The guard (lib/practice/guard.mjs:68) checks an affirmation as 'a human fork by the owner' into the Affirmed container, which is how 44a6f76d became f402de9a on 2026-10-29. So in a session the clerk must run `srs record fork <id> --into <Affirmed> --carry-relations outgoing` with the owner's SRS_ACTOR by hand, outside the session command and its dry run, and the session record does not list it as an act.
evidence: clerk lib/practice/guard.mjs:63-68: Affirmed members must be created by the owner's human actor (a fork)
srs-programme remedy f402de9a: createdBy github:the-greenman, derived-from 44a6f76d, answers 5d9b77b6 and 61784feb carried (2026-10-29)
Ad hoc session 2026-11-03 22:14 UTC: remedy 6848d96e affirmed this way

Also noted: the session agenda warns 'no status-quo option' on D1-D3 (73dba259, 9c116ddb, 287c64f4) although each has an option lettered 'A. Status quo' / 'A. No examples'; the check matches the option's name, not its letter-prefixed form
fieldValues.body:
- The act exists in the guard and in practice but not in the session command, so it is neither dry-run nor minuted: the session record says what was ratified, not what was affirmed.
- What to do instead: `clerk session --affirm <id>` that forks into Affirmed as the owner's actor, carries outgoing relations, and lists the act in the session record; until then run the fork by hand in the session copy before the session command so one PR carries both, and name it in the session summary.
- The status-quo warning is a parser nit: either accept a letter prefix, or the 7b91246b shape says the status-quo option is named 'Status quo' exactly.
